qCGofLIzX6g.summary: Armin Ronacher, creator of Flask, explains how CPython's internals and C API leak into the language's semantics. Using examples like the complexity of the add operation, he shows why Python is hard to optimize or reimplement.
qCGofLIzX6g.why: It is HN's standard answer to why Python cannot easily get much faster, and is recommended by people who work on JITs and alternative runtimes.

qv6UVOQ0F44.summary: SethBling shows MarI/O, a program using neural networks and the NEAT genetic algorithm to learn to play Super Mario World. The description links the source code, the paper and background reading.
qv6UVOQ0F44.why: The go-to accessible introduction to neuroevolution and NEAT, praised for crediting prior research.

qJEWOTZnFeg.summary: A long interview by Blender Guru with Ton Roosendaal, creator of Blender. They cover Blender's origins, the move to open source, why Ton is not driven by money, Autodesk, and what sets Blender apart from other open source projects.
qJEWOTZnFeg.why: Recommended as the best account of Blender's history and its user-focused approach as a free software success story.

qI_g07C_Q5I.summary: Martin Fowler's GOTO 2012 introduction to NoSQL databases: where they came from, their data models, how consistency thinking differs, and when to use them. He argues they won't make relational databases obsolete and introduces polyglot persistence.
qI_g07C_Q5I.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a balanced, beginner-friendly overview of SQL versus NoSQL, and some teachers assign it to students.

qd_hEja6bzE.summary: A feature-length film by the Makani team chronicling their thirteen-year effort to build energy kites that harvest wind power, with footage from test sites in Hawaii, California and Norway. It shows the engineering, the team and the eventual shutdown.
qd_hEja6bzE.why: HN recommends it as a technically rich, beautifully made documentary on ambitious hardware engineering and failure.

q5SRrsr-Iug.summary: Bret Weinstein and Yuri Deigin discuss the evidence for the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 leaked from a lab, including the furin cleavage site and gain-of-function research. The conversation draws on Deigin's Medium article.
q5SRrsr-Iug.why: HN commenters shared it in 2020 and 2021 as an early, in-depth presentation of the lab-leak case, though it is a contested viewpoint.

qEV9qoup2mQ.summary: CGP Grey tells the story of Alexander Pope's long takedown of a historian, Thomas Hearne, framed around the quirks of library books and archival research. It is a funny, digressive video essay about literary feuds and tracking down original sources.
qEV9qoup2mQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a masterpiece of humorous archival detective work and a great watch about books and libraries.

qbIk7-JPB2c.summary: Sebastien Bubeck presents the Sparks of AGI paper at MIT, showing early experiments with GPT-4 across many domains and asking whether artificial intelligence has arrived. It includes the TikZ unicorn example.
qbIk7-JPB2c.why: HN recommends it as a thought-provoking talk from a researcher with early GPT-4 access, especially for the unicorn degrading under safety tuning.

qp0HIF3SfI4.summary: Simon Sinek's TED talk presents the 'golden circle' model: great leaders and companies inspire action by starting with why they do something, before how or what. He illustrates it with Apple, Martin Luther King, the Wright brothers and, as a counterexample, TiVo.
qp0HIF3SfI4.why: HN commenters cite it to explain why customers buy into a company's beliefs rather than its specs, especially in threads about Apple, marketing and product messaging.

qsEjV8DdSbs.summary: Mick West analyzes the Navy's Gimbal UFO video and gives four checkable observations suggesting it is an infrared glare that appears to rotate because the camera rotates while tracking. He argues the object is likely a hot craft hidden behind the glare.
qsEjV8DdSbs.why: Pointed to as the clearest, evidence-based debunk of the Gimbal footage, and a model of how to analyze such claims.

qybUFnY7Y8w.summary: OK Go's music video for This Too Shall Pass, featuring a huge Rube Goldberg machine built in a warehouse in Los Angeles with Syyn Labs. The band interacts with the contraption in one continuous take.
qybUFnY7Y8w.why: HN points to it as an example of ambitious, practical-effects creativity in music videos, made without CGI.

qID2B4MK7Y0.summary: jan Misali presents an humorous but earnest case for counting in base 6 (seximal) instead of base 10 or 12, comparing the arithmetic advantages of each.
qID2B4MK7Y0.why: HN points to it as a funny, convincing take on number bases whenever dozenal or base 6 comes up.

q_vivC7c_1k.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment arguing that tipping should be banned. It covers the history of tipping, its weak link to service quality, and why employers should pay a fair wage.
q_vivC7c_1k.why: Recommended in tipping threads as a fast, entertaining, sourced case against tipping culture.

qOP2V_np2c0.summary: An RSA Animate video that illustrates a talk by geographer David Harvey on the crises of capitalism. It covers creative destruction, wage stagnation masked by credit, and the search for a more just economic order.
qOP2V_np2c0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a quick animated introduction to Harvey's and Marx's critique of capitalism.

q7K0vRUKXKc.summary: Paul Graham speaks at Startup School 2008 about how to create a successful startup. His talk emphasizes being good, not just avoiding being evil, as a strategic advantage.
q7K0vRUKXKc.why: HN points to it as a staple pg talk, and it appears in lists of the best startup videos and tech talks.

qOTYgcdNrXE.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explains Multi-Domain Operations through footage from his last mission at RIMPAC 2018. He covers missile and torpedo testing and interviews military leaders about the cyber and information domains.
qOTYgcdNrXE.why: HN cites it for an insider's look at defense work and at how the military thinks about information operations and cyberspace.

qTBAW-Eh0tM.summary: Tom Scott-style exploration by suckerpinch (Tom7) of generalized anagrams where letters can be broken into pieces, called anagraphs, with a whimsical computational approach.
qTBAW-Eh0tM.why: HN recommends it as a typical example of Tom7's technically astounding and playful videos.

qhbuKbxJsk8.summary: Mathologer shows how times table diagrams on a circle produce cardioids and other curves connected to the Mandelbrot set. He explains the patterns and links to a tool for making your own diagrams.
qhbuKbxJsk8.why: HN recommends it as the clearest explanation of the patterns behind modular multiplication diagrams and times table art.

q0RX59G2jaA.summary: A day-in-the-life video following a move between apartments in Tokyo using a Japanese moving company. It shows how the movers work and what the experience is like.
q0RX59G2jaA.why: Commenters recommend it for the movers' rigor and discipline, which they find oddly satisfying to watch.

qE7dYhpI_bI.summary: Adam Savage shows a set of Mitutoyo ceramic gauge blocks and uses them to explain metrology, the science of measurement. He argues that accuracy and precision work differently than most people assume, which changes how you think about every measuring tool.
qE7dYhpI_bI.why: Recommended as a thoughtful, enjoyable 45-minute dive into measurement and the appreciation of precision.

qH6sSOr-yk8.summary: Sean Parent's GoingNative 2013 talk surveys new and overlooked C++ features and shows how to use them for simple, correct, clear code. It stresses using standard algorithms rather than raw loops.
qH6sSOr-yk8.why: Recommended whenever the STL mindset or avoiding raw loops in C++ comes up, as an enlightening talk on expressive algorithms.

qJ7ZAUjsycY.summary: Scott Manley covers how GPS works and how civilian accuracy went from a planned 100 meters to about one meter. He explains the technology and the removal of restrictions that made this possible.
qJ7ZAUjsycY.why: Recommended as a solid history and explanation of GPS, especially when GPS outages or accuracy come up.

qPKj0YnKANw.summary: PBS Space Time explains Stephen Hawking's prediction of Hawking radiation and how black holes can emit radiation and slowly evaporate. It goes beyond the common particle-antiparticle analogy.
qPKj0YnKANw.why: Recommended as an accessible and correct explanation of Hawking radiation for non-physicists.

quLa6kzzra0.summary: Tony Chen of Microsoft explains at BlueHat Seattle 2019 how the Xbox One was designed to resist physical attacks. He covers the security design and hypervisor-based OS architecture that kept the console uncracked for years.
quLa6kzzra0.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating, authoritative account of console hardware security, often cited in threads on hardware security and anti-cheat.

qL0BB2PRY7k.summary: Practical Engineering compares modern concrete with that of the Roman Empire, covering modern techniques like roller compacted concrete and water-reducing admixtures. It explains the tradeoffs of Roman construction versus reinforced concrete.
qL0BB2PRY7k.why: HN recommends it as a clear, balanced answer to claims that Roman concrete was better than ours.

qMkYlIA7mgw.summary: CGP Grey walks through the odd history and quirks of the US-Canada border, including how it was surveyed and its irregularities such as exclaves.
qMkYlIA7mgw.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining overview in any thread about border oddities.

qQTjLWIHN74.summary: Wendover Productions explains why Amtrak trains run late: most Amtrak routes run on freight-owned track, and the law giving passenger trains priority is rarely enforced. The video covers rail ownership versus control and how freight carriers hold the leverage.
qQTjLWIHN74.why: HN commenters cite it whenever passenger rail delays or expansion come up, as the clearest explanation of freight priority over Amtrak.

qS34oV-jv_A.summary: Angela Collier, a physicist, revisits her earlier dark matter video, explaining dark matter as a set of observations rather than a theory and discussing MOND comments.
qS34oV-jv_A.why: HN points to her videos as a counterpoint to popular dark matter discussion, framing it as the discrepancy that needs explaining.

qbKGw8MQ0i8.summary: Robert Collins explains why rustup installs were painfully slow on Windows and how changes to rustup and Windows cut install time from 3m30s to 14s. The talk covers NTFS, small files and the cost of antivirus hooks on file close.
qbKGw8MQ0i8.why: The go-to reference for why file operations are slow on Windows and how antivirus filters, not NTFS itself, are the cause.

q3OuCR0EpGo.summary: A demo of the 8pen, a gesture-based keyboard replacement for touchscreens that lets users enter text by moving around a circle. It is meant for phones, remotes and game controllers and mimics handwriting.
q3OuCR0EpGo.why: HN commenters who used it remember it as an unusually fast and accurate touchscreen text input method and a fascinating alternative to QWERTY.

qEJ4hkpQW8E.summary: Scott Galloway's TED talk uses data to argue that young Americans are financially worse off than earlier generations, calling it a great intergenerational theft. He covers root causes and what could change it.
qEJ4hkpQW8E.why: HN commenters cite it for hard data on millennials versus boomers and the economic reality facing young workers.

qJZ1Ez28C-A.summary: A Veritasium video that follows the principle of least action from Bernoulli and Newton to quantum mechanics, asking whether light takes all possible paths at once. It includes experiments showing quantum waves.
qJZ1Ez28C-A.why: HN commenters call it eye-opening and deeper than typical layman explanations, linking it in double-slit and mechanics threads.

qPb_0JZ6-Rc.summary: Arthur Keller gives a roughly half-hour crash course on environmental collapse, covering exponential growth, carrying capacity and ecological overshoot.
qPb_0JZ6-Rc.why: HN commenters post it in climate threads as a clear explanation of overshoot and declining carrying capacity.

qoyKe-HxmFk.summary: Official trailer for the documentary Into Eternity, about Finland's Onkalo repository, built to store high-level nuclear waste safely for 100,000 years. It raises how to warn and communicate with far-future humans.
qoyKe-HxmFk.why: Recommended as a thought-provoking film on deep-time nuclear waste storage, though one commenter found it unenlightening.

q58dLWjRTBE.summary: Coffeezilla recounts being offered a $20k bounty to expose a Counter-Strike skin casino, then investigates and finds a different story. It is the first episode of a series on CS skin gambling.
q58dLWjRTBE.why: HN commenters recommend the series as an in-depth investigation of third-party skin gambling and Valve's response.

q9Golcxjpi8.summary: Ben Felix explains how to decide between renting and buying a home, weighing financial and non-financial factors. He argues that renting is often as good or better than owning, both financially and for well-being.
q9Golcxjpi8.why: Cited in housing threads for his rule-of-thumb rent-versus-buy analysis and the view that it is often a financial wash.

qLjgXPDzeZo.summary: A Dutch Top 2000 a gogo segment in which Norman Cook (Fatboy Slim) explains how The Rockafeller Skank is built, in his studio. The studio shows a long-running Atari ST setup.
qLjgXPDzeZo.why: HN links it mostly for the glimpse of Cook's studio and his decades-old Atari ST, and as an example of a sample-based track.

qSfdtmcZ4d0.summary: Rich Harris's Svelte Summit 2020 talk on what a modern web development workflow could look like. It announced that Sapper would give way to what became SvelteKit.
qSfdtmcZ4d0.why: Cited as the source for Sapper's end and SvelteKit's origin, and as an early view of where JS frameworks were heading.

qSjGouBmo0M.summary: John Green explains why the US spends far more on health care than other countries, going through insurers, drug companies, hospitals and lawyers. He argues the causes are complicated rather than a simple blame game.
qSjGouBmo0M.why: Pointed to as a quick, readable summary of the data behind US healthcare costs.

qWFScmtiC44.summary: Jonathan Blow gives a roughly 90-minute talk, followed by Q&A, on how video games could actually improve education, in contrast to what is currently being tried.
qWFScmtiC44.why: HN commenters find his insights good, especially the idea that games work for learning by doing and for teaching problem-solving, in contrast to gamification.

qWKz3psejb0.summary: Sal Mercogliano of What's Going on With Shipping? discusses a debate between the Center for Maritime Strategy and the Heritage Foundation over whether the Jones Act helps or harms American shipping and national security.
qWKz3psejb0.why: HN recommends the channel for clear coverage of the history, cabotage rules and debate around the Jones Act.

qZ73PftBfFg.summary: Lilium's CTO gives a short update on the electric jet's design, certification and development. It shows the canard and rear wing layout and the wheel design.
qZ73PftBfFg.why: Pointed to as primary-source company material that answers many engineering questions about the Lilium jet.

qgG5Jhi_Els.summary: A screencast showing how to use the fzf command-line fuzzy finder in the shell and in Vim. It covers searching files and also using the Vim plugin for help tags, buffers, lines and grep matches.
qgG5Jhi_Els.why: Recommended as a useful early tutorial for learning fzf with Vim.

qpoRO378qRY.summary: A 42-minute CBS interview with Geoffrey Hinton at the Vector Institute in 2023, covering the history of neural networks and the present and future of AI. He discusses AGI timelines and whether language models truly understand.
qpoRO378qRY.why: Recommended as a more nuanced look at Hinton's views than headlines, especially his argument that LLMs are more than auto-complete.

qs2QcycggWU.summary: Branch Education explains how Starlink works, from the ground dish and satellites to phased-array beam steering and data routing. Animations cover how a beam stays connected to a satellite moving at 27,000 km/h.
qs2QcycggWU.why: Recommended for its detailed and clear look at Starlink hardware and beamforming.

qv5b1Xowxdk.summary: A demonstration of loading Altair 4K BASIC on an Altair 8800 clone, using a front-panel bootloader and an ASR-33 Teletype. It shows the full sequence of entering boot code, loading BASIC and running a program.
qv5b1Xowxdk.why: Cited as a great demo of how early microcomputers were actually booted and operated.

qvNCVYkHKfg.summary: Yann LeCun on the Big Technology Podcast discusses why current AI models cannot make discoveries despite their knowledge. He argues systems need abstract world models and also covers limits of AI research, investor expectations, and open source after DeepSeek.
qvNCVYkHKfg.why: Pointed to as LeCun's argument for the limits of LLMs and the need for world models.

qB76jxBq_gQ.summary: Extracts from the documentary The Art of Piano showing Glenn Gould playing Bach's Partita No. 2.
qB76jxBq_gQ.why: HN uses it as a short introduction to Glenn Gould and his distinctive playing.

q2gO4DKVpa8.summary: Billionaire Nick Hanauer warns fellow wealthy people in a TED talk that growing inequality could lead to social upheaval like pre-revolutionary France. He argues a higher minimum wage would grow the middle class and prosperity.
q2gO4DKVpa8.why: HN brings it up in inequality, UBI and backlash threads as an early warning from a rich insider.

q4TZxj-Dq7s.summary: Netflix engineer Drew Gallatin explains why the company runs FreeBSD-current on its CDN. He describes the team, how they track upstream, their contributions and performance milestones, and a bug causing a 20% performance regression.
q4TZxj-Dq7s.why: HN cites it as the Netflix case for staying close to -CURRENT and upstreaming changes.

q5xvwPa3r7M.summary: Linus Tech Tips tests whether chaining many PCIe riser extensions causes loss of GPU performance. They keep adding extensions to see how far the signal will go.
q5xvwPa3r7M.why: HN cites it as empirical evidence that PCIe cables can be chained to roughly three meters before failing.

q7pI7IYaJLI.summary: A 47-minute documentary on Allan Savory and how he used Holistic Management to restore degraded land in Zimbabwe. It covers rotational grazing, soil health and regenerative agriculture.
q7pI7IYaJLI.why: Offered as further reading in threads about carbon removal, regenerative agriculture and holistic grazing.

qBpiXcyB7wU.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the state of the US power grid, why it needs fixing, and the risks of aging infrastructure.
qBpiXcyB7wU.why: Recommended as an entertaining primer on grid problems, and cited for aging equipment causing fires.

qS4H6PEcCCA.summary: Mathologer explains epicycles and complex Fourier series, inspired by an animation of Homer Simpson drawn with epicycles. It covers the shape of the Moon's orbit around the Sun and how to make your own epicycle drawings.
qS4H6PEcCCA.why: HN points to it as a visual teaching resource for Fourier series, and as a reference when epicycles come up as analogies.

qSfFq02pK4s.summary: A two-hour episode of Fall of Civilizations on the Nabataeans, from humble desert traders to masters of Petra, and what finally brought down their empire.
qSfFq02pK4s.why: HN mentions it for its stunning visuals of Petra and as background on Nabataean water engineering and history.

qWJpI2adCcs.summary: Mike Acton, in a HandmadeCon 2015 interview with Casey Muratori, discusses game engine development, hiring and learning on your own.
qWJpI2adCcs.why: HN cites it for Acton's common-sense views on building engines, valuing curiosity and self-driven learning.

qWKUFK7MWvg.summary: A short video accompanying the CVPR 2018 paper Learning to See in the Dark. It shows a neural network producing sharp images from very low-light raw sensor data, compared against denoising approaches.
qWKUFK7MWvg.why: HN commenters flag it as a remarkable machine-learning result, notably for showing that training on raw images beats JPEG.

qYiYd9RcK5M.summary: Ben Crystal performs Hamlet's 'To be, or not to be' in Original Pronunciation, the reconstructed accent of Shakespeare's time, on a London balcony.
qYiYd9RcK5M.why: HN uses it as the example of how different Shakespeare sounded in original pronunciation.

qrizmAo17Os.summary: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on homeowners associations, covering the surprising power they hold over residents and how arbitrary their rules can be. It mixes investigative comedy with examples of HOA overreach.
qrizmAo17Os.why: HN uses it as the go-to reference in threads about HOA absurdity, such as fines over small violations and authoritarian rules.

q3NQQ7bPf6U.summary: Tech Tangents sets up original Doom's three-screen multi-monitor mode, which required a separate networked computer for each monitor. The video covers the hardware and setup work and the result.
q3NQQ7bPf6U.why: HN references it as a demonstration of Doom's original multi-monitor support and as retro computing content.

q4DF3j4saCE.summary: A Kurzgesagt animation on supernovae, the most powerful explosions in the universe. It explains their role in creating elements and what would happen to Earth if one occurred nearby.
q4DF3j4saCE.why: HN cites it for how unlikely supernovae are as extinction events and how distance determines their impact.

qC5KtatMcUw.summary: Epic Games' reveal of Unreal Engine 5, a real-time demo running on PlayStation 5. It showcases Nanite virtualized micropolygon geometry and Lumen global illumination.
qC5KtatMcUw.why: HN cites it as a marker of where real-time graphics are heading, such as sub-pixel triangles and per-pixel compute.

qHepKd38pr0.summary: The Blade Runner scene in which Deckard uses a voice-controlled machine to enhance a photograph, zooming into hidden details.
qHepKd38pr0.why: Used as the canonical reference for the 'enhance' trope whenever image upscaling or recognition comes up.

qMGn9T37eR8.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the tension between public and private weather forecasting, including NOAA data and AccuWeather's lobbying against free public weather data.
qMGn9T37eR8.why: Routinely cited whenever US weather data, NOAA funding or privatization of forecasting comes up.

qNf9nzvnd1k.summary: A two-minute sine tone sweeping exponentially from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, covering the human hearing range at constant acoustic pressure.
qNf9nzvnd1k.why: Used as a quick hearing-range test and as a tone source for tinnitus experiments.

qOt7xDKxmCM.summary: A long documentary-style film on the 1961 SL-1 reactor accident, where a control rod was withdrawn too far and the reactor went prompt-critical. The resulting steam explosion ejected control rods and shield plugs.
qOt7xDKxmCM.why: HN links it in nuclear safety and military reactor discussions as the full story of the only fatal US reactor accident.

qQkx-4pFjus.summary: Dashcam footage of a Tesla Model S on adaptive cruise control hitting a stopped van, with the driver listing the safety systems that failed to react. The uploader still calls the Model S the best car in the world.
qQkx-4pFjus.why: Cited in Autopilot threads as an example of Tesla driver-assist systems rear-ending stationary vehicles.

qXD9HnrNrvk.summary: A roughly three-minute Onion News Network satire in which a host consoles a severely depressed zoologist who spent his whole life studying anteaters. It is a short comedy sketch about wasted effort and misplaced obsession.
qXD9HnrNrvk.why: Commenters bring it up as a joke when a thread touches on long-term commitment, obscure specialization, or someone devoting a lifetime to something niche.

q_A1GNx0M9M.summary: A one-minute clip of the Warcraft II sound card test in setup, where the test sample plays and the voice says the sound card works perfectly.
q_A1GNx0M9M.why: Quoted as a nostalgic joke about DOS-era game setup.

qaHLd8de6nM.summary: A Guardian clip of Barack Obama at the Obama Foundation summit saying that call-out culture is not activism and that casting stones will not bring change.
qaHLd8de6nM.why: Cited repeatedly in threads on wokeness, cancel culture and outrage as an authoritative voice from the left criticizing call-outs.

qdFLPn30dvQ.summary: A short clip from Animal House of Kevin Bacon's character at a fraternity paddling, saying 'Thank you sir, may I have another?'
qdFLPn30dvQ.why: Used only as a joke reply, typically when someone willingly accepts punishment or abuse.

qf7ws2DF-zk.summary: Veritasium explains why no voting system can be perfectly fair, drawing on Arrow's theorem and the work of Eric Maskin. It looks at problems with systems like first-past-the-post and ranked-choice voting.
qf7ws2DF-zk.why: Linked when someone needs a quick accessible source for the claim that every voting method has flaws.

qfv6Ah_MVJU.summary: A compilation of Apple's 'I'm a Mac, I'm a PC' ad campaign from 2006 onward.
qfv6Ah_MVJU.why: Cited as an example of pointed comparative advertising and for how Apple's claims, such as virus-free and fewer pop-ups, have aged.

qoIvd3zzu4Y.summary: The business card scene from the film American Psycho, in which executives compare increasingly refined business cards with escalating envy. It is a two-minute clip of a classic dark comedy moment.
qoIvd3zzu4Y.why: Used as a joke reference for obsessing over trivial details like card design, fonts and CV templates.

qp75-46PnMY.summary: CityNerd's Ray Delahanty tallies the personal costs of driving and then the externalities that car dependency imposes on everyone else, with numbers for each. It is an urbanist case that driving is heavily subsidized and costs society far more than drivers pay.
qp75-46PnMY.why: HN commenters cite it as the video version of the research on the social cost of driving when arguing cars impose uncompensated costs on others.

qrwlk7_GF9g.summary: A Russian-language investigation by Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation into Dmitry Medvedev's alleged corruption network. It documents charities funding palaces, vineyards and yachts, and has English subtitles available.
qrwlk7_GF9g.why: HN cites it as a well-documented investigation into Russian elite corruption and as evidence of Navalny's influence.

qvNLNl7oJnM.summary: Rhonda Patrick gives an IHMC talk on how genetic variation affects micronutrient absorption and metabolism, and how diet changes gene expression. It also covers epigenetics, including heritable changes, and stress tolerance.
qvNLNl7oJnM.why: Cited as a reference in threads on telomeres, lifespan extension and longevity research funding, mainly for the nutrigenomics and epigenetics material.

qy8MdewY_TY.summary: PBS Space Time asks whether dark matter could be made of primordial black holes. It walks through the observational constraints that limit this idea.
qy8MdewY_TY.why: HN people link it in dark matter and black hole threads as a clear summary of why black holes alone are unlikely to explain dark matter.

qycUOENFIBs.summary: A one-minute clip of Steve Ballmer laughing at the original iPhone and dismissing its price and appeal.
qycUOENFIBs.why: HN uses it as a joke or cautionary reference when a company or analyst confidently dismisses a product that later succeeds.
